subject.title: [Bug]: Memory Multimodal Indexing - Gemini API rejects OGG/Opus audio files

question: Should Gemini multimodal memory skip/report unsupported OGG/Opus audio, or should OpenClaw transcode it to MP3/WAV before embedding?
rationale: Both choices are technically plausible, but they set different public support, dependency, operator, cost, and maintenance contracts for memory audio.

options.title: Filter And Diagnose
options.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV-only Gemini audio, with OGG/Opus producing a clear non-fatal skip or diagnostic instead of a provider 400.

options.title: Own Transcoding
options.body: Reuse or extend the existing ffmpeg-backed media infrastructure to convert unsupported audio to a Gemini-supported format, with dependency detection and failure handling.

options.title: Defer To Multimodal Plan
options.body: Keep this under broader multimodal memory direction until provider-specific media handling is settled across formats.

recommendation.title: Filter And Diagnose
recommendation.body: Document and enforce MP3/WAV-only Gemini audio, with OGG/Opus producing a clear non-fatal skip or diagnostic instead of a provider 400.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision lands closest to the shipped multimodal memory extraPaths boundary introduced in their merged work.
